question_set_contract.dependency_contract: Exactly two questions use Lesson 4: q01 direct retrieval and q07 mixed stress-strain/Young-modulus application.
question_set_contract.difficulty_progression: definition and ratio to graph gradient and independently checked multi-route calculation

questions.prompt: Define tensile stress and tensile strain.
Define Young modulus and state its SI unit.
A material has tensile stress 6.0 × 10⁷ Pa at tensile strain 3.0 × 10⁻⁴. What is its Young modulus?
On the same stress-strain axes, material P has a steeper proportional line than material Q. Which statement is correct?

options.A: P has smaller Young modulus and is less stiff.
options.B: P has larger Young modulus and is stiffer.
options.C: Both have the same Young modulus.

questions.prompt: Two wires are made from the same material but have different lengths and areas. Which quantity should be the same while both behave proportionally?

The proportional stress-strain data for a material include the points (strain, stress/Pa): (0,0), (2.0 × 10⁻⁴, 3.2 × 10⁷), (4.0 × 10⁻⁴, 6.4 × 10⁷), (6.0 × 10⁻⁴, 9.6 × 10⁷). Plot stress against strain on the unlabeled grid, draw the proportional line, and calculate Young modulus from a large gradient triangle. Explain what the gradient means physically.

questions.prompt: A wire of original length 1.80 m and cross-sectional area 3.00 × 10⁻⁷ m² carries a tensile force of 45.0 N and extends by 1.50 mm in the proportional region. Calculate tensile stress, tensile strain and Young modulus. Use a second route to check E and compare the material with one whose Young modulus is 1.20 × 10¹¹ Pa.
